@@ -18,9 +18,13 @@ The Ignite Cache endpoint is one of camel-ignite endpoints that allow you to int
This offers both a Producer (to invoke cache operations on an Ignite cache) and a Consumer (to consume changes from a continuous query).
The cache value is the body of the message, and the cache key is in the `CamelIgniteCacheKey` message header.
-GET and REMOVE take the key from the body when that header is not set, and a PUT of a `Map` body puts all its entries.
+GET and REMOVE take the key from the body when that header is not set.
+A PUT of a `Map` body without that header puts all its entries; with the header, or with `treatCollectionsAsCacheObjects=true`, the `Map` is stored as one value.
Even if you configure a fixed operation in the endpoint URI, you can vary it per-exchange by setting the `CamelIgniteCacheOperation` message header.
+Without either, the producer fails.

+With `fireExistingQueryResults=true`, the consumer first sends the entries that the initial query finds, each with the value as the body and the key in the `CamelIgniteCacheKey` header, like the events that follow.
// component options: START
include::partial$component-configure-options.adoc[]
@@ -41,6 +41,9 @@ Each operation expects the indicated types:
| AFFINITY_RUN | IgniteRunnable.
+Without a body the producer fails, except EXECUTE with the `taskName` option, which then passes the `CamelIgniteComputeParameters` header to the task.
+RUN and AFFINITY_RUN have no result: they keep the body, or leave no body when `propagateIncomingBodyIfNoReturnValue` is `false`.
== Usage
The component needs an Ignite node: xref:ignite-summary.adoc[Ignite] describes the ways to give it one.
The Ignite ID Generator endpoint is one of camel-ignite endpoints that allow you to interact with https://apacheignite.readme.io/docs/id-generator[Ignite Atomic Sequences and ID Generators].
+`ADD_AND_GET` and `GET_AND_ADD` add the number in the body to the sequence, and fail without a body.
+The other operations do not use the body.
+The operation is the `operation` option, or the `CamelIgniteIdGenOperation` header; without either, the producer fails.

+The operation is the `operation` option, or the `CamelIgniteQueueOperation` header; without either, the producer fails.
